title: Prevalence and Subtypes of Human Herpesvirus 8 in People Living with HIV as Predictors of HHV-8-Associated Lymphoproliferative Disorders, Malignancies, and Inflammatory Manifestations: A Combined Seroprevalence and Multicenter Cohort Study to Identify Diagnostic Gaps
summary:
Human herpesvirus 8 belongs to the family of herpesviruses and, in most cases, does not cause disease after infection. However, when a condition such as HIV is present and the immune system is weakened, various diseases may develop.

It is currently unknown how many people living with HIV in Germany are also infected with human herpesvirus 8. It is also unclear why some people develop disease while others do not.

This study aims to determine how many people living with HIV are additionally infected with human herpesvirus 8. It will also investigate whether certain viral variants are associated with more severe disease courses.

For this purpose, blood samples from people living with HIV will be tested for antibodies against human herpesvirus 8. In an additional step, blood samples from people living with HIV who have a disease caused by human herpesvirus 8 will be analysed.

interventions.name: For the seroprevalence part of the study, blood samples from 5,000 people living with HIV will be evaluated.

In the multicenter component of the study, associations between HHV-8 subtypes, epidemiological factors, and laboratory parameters will be assessed in an estimated 100 PLHIV with HHV-8-associated diseases.

criteria:
Inclusion criteria:
For the multicentre component: Written informed consent from patients.
Exclusion criteria:
For the multicentre component: Missing informed consent.
